name: finance
title: Finance
summary: Seller money and company money kept apart: the seller ledger (proceeds, pending, available, held, negative and amounts owed), fee rules, holds, adjustments, payout runs and payouts, statements, payout-destination verification, daily reconciliation checks, and company trading margins separate from marketplace fee income.
owns: Seller ledger: append-only entries for sales, shipping charged, seller-funded discounts, marketplace fees, refunds (including refund after payout), holds and releases, adjustments, ad charges, label charges and payouts
Seller balances: sales proceeds, pending, available, held (each hold with reason and review date), negative balance and amounts owed

Fee rules with versions and effective dates: commission basis (before or after discounts), shipping included or not, platform- vs seller-funded discounts, category rates, fee treatment for cancellations, returns and payment disputes
Fee charge per order item, computed at sale and reversed in proportion on refund
Holds: manual and rule-based (chargeback, dispute, unconfirmed delivery, new seller, restriction), release, extension and application
Adjustments with reason codes, recorded owner and second-reviewer approval above a threshold
Payout schedule, payout runs (second Finance reviewer above a threshold), payouts (Pending, Processing, Paid, Failed) and failed-payout recovery
Payout destination verification and change review before money goes to a new account
Itemised seller statements that reconcile to the payout
Company trading (Official Store product sales, buying cost, discounts, shipping expense, returns and write-offs, margin) reported separately from marketplace fee income
Daily reconciliation checks (payments vs orders, seller amounts vs statements, provider deposits, unexplained amounts, failed payouts) with recorded reasons for corrections
notOwns: Charging customers, executing refunds and chargeback cases: payments (finance books their results)
Refund decisions and approvals for returns and case remedies: returns (finance reads returns.refund.approved for the funding split)
Seller payout account details and owner-only change requests: sellers (finance verifies and reviews the change before paying to it)
Approval limits and second-reviewer requests: access
Ad campaign billing rules: advertising (finance posts the charges it is given)
Report definitions and exports: reports (reads finance read models)

publicApi.name: recordServiceFee
publicApi.signature: (input: { sellerId: uuid, amount: Money, kind: string, reference: Reference, description: string, idempotencyKey: string }) => LedgerEntry
publicApi.desc: Posts a fulfillment-service fee (storage, handling, receiving, returns processing, removal; kind = the FeeCharge type) to the seller ledger as service_fee, kept separate from commission and ad charges. Same idempotencyKey returns the first entry.

publicApi.name: creditSellerCharge
publicApi.signature: (input: { sellerId: uuid, amount: Money, originalEntryId: uuid, reason: string, idempotencyKey: string }) => LedgerEntry
publicApi.desc: Credits back all or part of an ad charge or service fee (originalEntryId = the LedgerEntry returned by recordAdCharge or recordServiceFee) as charge_credit; never more than the original minus earlier credits. Same idempotencyKey returns the first entry.

publicApi.name: creditSeller
publicApi.signature: (input: { sellerId: uuid, amount: Money, reason: string, reference: Reference, idempotencyKey: string }) => SellerCredit
publicApi.desc: Credits a seller without an original charge (fulfillment-service reimbursements for lost or damaged units, goodwill to a seller) as ledger type seller_credit. Up to creditSecondReviewerThreshold it is posted at once (status posted, ledgerEntry set). Above it the credit waits as pending_approval with an approval request (finance.credits.issue) and is posted or rejected on access.approval.decided, publishing finance.seller_credit.decided. Same idempotencyKey returns the first credit.

publicApi.name: getSellerCredit
publicApi.signature: (by: { creditId?: uuid, idempotencyKey?: string }) => SellerCredit | null
publicApi.desc: Current state of a credit asked for with creditSeller (posted, pending_approval, rejected or withdrawn), by id or by the caller's idempotency key; replaces re-calling creditSeller to read it back

publicApi.name: withdrawSellerCredit
publicApi.signature: (input: { creditId?: uuid, idempotencyKey?: string, reason: string }) => SellerCredit
publicApi.desc: Withdraws a credit still pending_approval (e.g. the reimbursement it pays was reversed): status withdrawn, its approval request is cancelled through access, nothing is posted. A posted credit is refused with ILLEGAL_TRANSITION (reverse it with an adjustment); withdrawing a withdrawn credit returns it unchanged

publicApi.name: recordExternalDifference
publicApi.signature: (input: { check: 'store_credit', subject: string, description: string, expected: Money, actual: Money, reference?: Reference, key: string }) => ReconItem
publicApi.desc: Another module reports a money difference it found in its own books for the daily check (wallet: a customer balance that differs from its ledger sum). Creates an open reconciliation item on today's day for check store_credit (finance.reconciliation.mismatch_found); the same key returns the existing item, and a later report with expected = actual matches it (finance.reconciliation.item_closed)

publicApi.name: recordCompanyCost

stateMachines.name: Earnings lot
stateMachines.notes: makeAvailable runs when the item is delivered and the hold window (availableAfterDeliveryDays) has passed. A refund after paid_out does not touch the lot: it is a refund_after_payout ledger entry that can make the balance negative. A failed payout returns its lots to available.

stateMachines.name: Hold
stateMachines.notes: Every hold has a reason and a review date shown to the seller. apply turns the held amount into a deduction (e.g. chargeback lost) with a reason. Placing or releasing above the approver's hold limit needs an access approval.

stateMachines.name: Payout run
stateMachines.notes: A run above the first approver's finance.payouts.release limit (access) needs a second, different Finance approver (access approval request for the second). Approved is not paid: release sends each pending payout to the provider (processing). complete runs when every payout is paid, failed or cancelled.

stateMachines.name: Payout
stateMachines.notes: Plan ch. 14 payout statuses. Paid only when the provider confirms the deposit. A failed payout returns its money to the seller's available balance (payout_returned entry); recovery creates a new payout (retryOf) after the destination is fixed and verified. Payouts only go to a verified destination.

stateMachines.name: Destination review
stateMachines.notes: Created when sellers publishes sellers.payout_account.changed. Checks: micro-deposits (confirm-deposits), owner re-authentication, callback to the registered phone (the reviewer records it with callbackConfirmed on approve; verify is refused with CHECKS_INCOMPLETE until all three passed). Payouts keep going to the current verified account until verify; payouts to the new one wait at least destinationChangePauseHours.

stateMachines.name: Fee rule set
stateMachines.notes: Proposed by the Platform Administrator or Finance, approved by the Business Owner (access). Fees on an order item use the version active when the order was accepted.

stateMachines.name: Adjustment
stateMachines.notes: Within the recorder's finance.adjustments.record limit (access) an adjustment is recorded at once; above it it waits for a second Finance reviewer.

stateMachines.name: Seller credit
stateMachines.notes: creditSeller posts credits up to creditSecondReviewerThreshold at once (created posted). Larger credits wait for finance.credits.issue and finish on access.approval.decided. withdraw (withdrawSellerCredit, by the module that asked for the credit) cancels the approval request; an approval decided after a withdrawal posts nothing.

stateMachines.name: Reconciliation item
stateMachines.notes: explain records a reason when no money needs to move (timing, provider fee). Corrections above the caller's correction limit (access) need a second reviewer; applying one posts the matching entry (refund via payments, seller adjustment, write-off).

stateMachines.name: Amount owed
stateMachines.notes: Created when a negative balance is not covered within negativeBalanceOwedAfterDays. New earnings offset it first. Write-off needs a reason and, above the caller's limit, a second Finance reviewer: the pending write-off is kept on the record (pendingWriteOff, approval) until decided.

stateMachines.name: Statement
stateMachines.notes: The open statement of a period exists from the seller's approval (or the previous statement's issue); issued at the payout cutoff and immutable afterwards.

consumes.name: orders.order.accepted
consumes.does: Create pending earnings lots and fee charges per seller item (sale, shipping charged, seller-funded discount, fee); Official Store items go to trading_entries

consumes.name: orders.item.cancelled
consumes.does: Reverse the lot; apply the cancellation fee treatment

consumes.name: orders.item.delivered
consumes.does: Start the availability clock for the item's lot

consumes.name: payments.payment.captured
consumes.does: Record collected money for reconciliation (payments vs orders): card amount plus creditAmount (store credit) per capture, including captures with amount 0 for orders or groups paid entirely by store credit; the daily check compares card captures plus credit with the order total less cancelled items, so mixed and credit-only payments are not mismatches

consumes.name: returns.refund.approved
consumes.does: Store the funding split (seller, platform, shared) for the refund

consumes.name: payments.refund.sent
consumes.does: Post the refund and proportional fee refund to the seller ledger (refund_after_payout when the lot was paid out) or to company trading

consumes.name: payments.chargeback.opened
consumes.does: Place a chargeback hold on the seller (fee kept while open per fee treatment)

consumes.name: payments.chargeback.decided
consumes.does: won: release the chargeback hold. lost: apply the hold as a chargeback deduction from the seller (or a company trading loss for Official Store orders) and record the fee treatment

consumes.name: returns.label.created
consumes.does: Return labels: charge a seller-paid label to the seller, record a platform shipping expense, or nothing when the customer pays (deducted from the refund). Keyed by labelId

consumes.name: shipping.label.purchased
consumes.does: Outbound and replacement labels: charge seller-bought labels to the seller ledger, record company labels as Official Store shipping expense and platform labels as platform cost. kind = return is ignored (booked from returns.label.created)

consumes.name: shipping.label.voided
consumes.does: Reverse the charge or expense booked for that labelId (any kind)

consumes.name: shipping.claim.status_changed
consumes.does: paid: credit paidAmount to whoever bore the loss (seller ledger or company trading); other statuses are kept for reconciliation

consumes.name: promotions.coupon.redeemed
consumes.does: Record discount funding (platform vs seller) for fee basis and discount reports

consumes.name: promotions.redemption.reversed
consumes.does: Reverse the recorded discount funding (platform and seller parts) for the order item, so fee basis and discount reports match after a cancellation or refund

consumes.name: payments.refund.failed
consumes.does: Mark the refund's stored funding split failed (nothing is posted until payments.refund.sent); on the final attempt list it in the daily reconciliation

consumes.name: sellers.seller.approved
consumes.does: Open the seller account and apply the new-seller hold rule

consumes.name: sellers.seller.suspended
consumes.does: Put the seller's pending payouts on hold with reason restriction (review date from the restriction)

consumes.name: sellers.seller.closed
consumes.does: Issue a final statement and schedule the last payout after open obligations

consumes.name: sellers.payout_account.changed
consumes.does: Open a destination review; keep paying the current verified destination

consumes.name: access.approval.decided
consumes.does: Finish approval-required holds, adjustments, corrections, payout runs, fee rule changes and seller credits (finance.credits.issue: post or reject, publish finance.seller_credit.decided)

consumes.name: support.case.decided
consumes.does: Release or apply dispute holds linked to the case

consumes.name: wallet.credit.granted
consumes.does: Phase 3: record the store-credit liability (refund to credit, goodwill, gift cards). Only kind goodwill with chargedTo platform is booked as a platform cost; chargedTo seller is posted to the seller's earnings

consumes.name: wallet.credit.used
consumes.does: Phase 3: reduce the store-credit liability when credit pays for an order

consumes.name: wallet.credit.reversed
consumes.does: Phase 3: a goodwill grant was reversed (unused credit removed): reduce the store-credit liability by the amount; chargedTo seller: credit the seller back the goodwill charge posted for the grant (keyed by grantEntryId, never more than was charged); chargedTo platform: reduce the platform goodwill cost. Keyed by entryId

consumes.name: wallet.credit.expired
consumes.does: Phase 3: unused credit expired: reduce the store-credit liability (expired credit is recorded as platform breakage, not seller money). Keyed by entryId

consumes.name: wallet.credit.corrected
consumes.does: Phase 3: staff corrected a balance: increase (positive) or reduce (negative) the store-credit liability, booked as a platform credit correction with the reason. Keyed by entryId

jobs.name: finance.payout-run.create
jobs.does: Checks the payoutSchedule cutoff itself (e.g. Thu 23:59 market time before a Friday payout): once the latest cutoff has passed and no run exists for it, issue statements for the period and create the draft payout run. Idempotent per cutoff (RUN_ALREADY_EXISTS-safe), so a late or repeated run, or a restart after the cutoff, creates exactly one run. Also opens the current period's statement for seller accounts that have none (statements are never created on read)

jobs.name: finance.payout-run.release

jobs.name: finance.negative-balance.age

jobs.name: finance.fee-rules.activate

DESTINATION_NOT_VERIFIED.meaning: The seller has no verified payout destination; money stays in the balance.

SAME_APPROVER.meaning: The second approval must come from a different person than the first approver or the requester.

RUN_ALREADY_EXISTS.meaning: A payout run already exists for this cutoff. details.runId.

PAYOUT_NOT_RETRYABLE.meaning: Only failed payouts without an open retry can be retried.

STATEMENT_NOT_READY.meaning: The statement period is still open.

CHECKS_INCOMPLETE.meaning: Destination verification checks are not all passed. details.pending.

DEPOSIT_AMOUNTS_INCORRECT.meaning: The amounts do not match the test deposits. details.attemptsLeft.

DEPOSIT_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED.meaning: No tries left; new test deposits must be sent.

RECON_DAY_INCOMPLETE.meaning: Open mismatches remain; explain or correct them first. details.openItems.

notes: Fulfilled by Marketly money (decision D1, no finance change): the seller stays the seller of record, so the sale and the shipping charge stay in the seller's proceeds as for any seller group; the outbound label the warehouse buys for a marketly_service group is billedTo seller and booked from shipping.label.purchased like a seller-bought label; Fulfilled by Marketly fees arrive through recordServiceFee (service_fee, fulfillment section of the statement) and reimbursements through creditSeller / creditSellerCharge; refunds of Fulfilled by Marketly returns are seller-funded like other seller returns.

Seller ledger exports run through reports like every other export: POST /api/seller/finance/ledger/exports creates a finance.seller.ledger job (date range; columns: date, entry type, order or payout reference, description, amount, balance after) and GET /ledger/exports/{id} returns its status and link.

The ledger is append-only and the source of truth; seller_accounts is a projection. Every entry references the record that caused it (order, return, refund, case, chargeback, payout, adjustment, ad campaign).

Seller money and company money never mix: Official Store sales go to trading_entries and company trading reports, never to a seller payout. Marketplace seller sales are not company revenue; only the fee portion is marketplace income.

Fee example (illustration only): an eligible $100 item sale with a 10% fee creates $10 of fee income and $90 of seller earnings before other adjustments. Default rules: commission on item price after seller-funded discounts, shipping excluded, platform-funded discounts do not lower seller proceeds. Category rates are examples (Electronics 8%, Computers 7%, Home & Kitchen 12%, Fashion 15%, Sports 10%, Beauty 12%).

Refund after payout: the refund is deducted from later earnings (refund_after_payout entry); if the balance stays negative for negativeBalanceOwedAfterDays it becomes an amount owed. Statements show the deduction with the original payout reference (acceptance scenario 6).
Ad charges are separate ledger entries and a separate statement section, never part of commission.

Approvals (decision F-D1: limits come from access only): holds, adjustments, corrections, write-offs, payout runs and fee rule changes check the caller's limit through access (seller credits from creditSeller use creditSecondReviewerThreshold, since the caller is a module); above it the record is saved pending and the endpoint answers its normal status with `approval` in the body (FORMAT.md, Approval responses), finishing on access.approval.decided. The former runSecondReviewerThreshold, adjustmentSecondReviewerThreshold and correctionSecondReviewerThreshold settings are removed (their stored values are deleted by the settings module); the example amounts live in the access limits seed. Staff access to finance screens is not financial authority: approve endpoints need finance.payouts.approve and a limit.

Marketplace facts have their own tables, never trading_entries: captures (payments captured, card and store credit), discount_funding (coupon platform and seller parts), platform_costs (labels, refund shares, carrier claims, goodwill credit, credit corrections and breakage, written-off seller debts) and store_credit_liability. trading_entries holds Official Store trading only.

Store credit liability (phase 3): finance keeps the liability (store_credit_liability) from wallet events: granted adds, used, reversed and expired reduce, corrected adds or reduces (each keyed by the wallet entry id). A reversed seller-charged goodwill grant credits the seller back the charge posted for it. The daily store_credit check compares the liability with wallet.getLiabilityTotal and lists per-account differences wallet reports through recordExternalDifference.

New-seller period: when sellers.seller.approved is consumed the seller account gets new_seller_until (today + newSellerPeriodDays) and new_seller_extra_days (recommendedHoldDays, else newSellerHoldDays). Items delivered up to that day become available that many extra days later. It is shown in SettlementRules, not as a hold.

Statements: a seller's open statement is created when the seller is approved and, for the next period, when a statement is issued (finance.payout-run.create also opens one for any seller account that has none); reading statements never creates one.

Trust holds: a hold placed for a trust recommendation (HoldInput.trustReportId) keeps holds.trust_report_id through an approval, so finance.hold.placed carries trustReportId when the approved hold is finally placed and trust can confirm the hold_payout action.
Payout destination details belong to sellers (owner-only changes); finance stores only a label, provider destination id and verification state, and never pays an unverified destination.
Chargeback cases themselves are in payments; finance holds the seller amount and applies or releases it when payments reports the outcome.
Dependency note: returns, advertising, promotions, purchasing, inventory, shipping and support are optional inputs; without them their lines are simply absent from statements and trading.

Micro-deposit verification: the payout provider sends the two test deposits to the new destination and checks the amounts the owner enters (POST /api/seller/finance/payout-destination/confirm-deposits); finance moves no money for the check and records only the result on the destination review.
